title: Graveyard continuity roundup — Apr 05 2026
content:
Shift: Graveyard (00:00 - 08:00 UTC) — primary oncall: Avery Patel (pager)

Summary (TL;DR):
- Two attention events during the shift. Neither reached customer-facing outage SLA but both produced elevated latency and 5xx rates for a subset of inference traffic.
- Mitigations applied (automatic fallback + temporary capacity bump) restored baseline traffic within ~12 minutes for the first event and ~9 minutes for the second.
- We have three follow-ups: (1) clear root cause for short-lived KV cache/eviction storm, (2) refine the request-sampling probe for rapid detection, (3) small runbook clarifications for dedupe of fallback routing.

Detailed timeline:
- 01:10 UTC: Alert P1-ish: increase in p95 latency and request error rate on hosted-api-us-central route.
  - Symptoms: p95 latency jumped from ~120ms to ~900ms, 5xx rate from 0.2% to 3.8% on endpoint model-redwood/gpt-medium-q4.
  - First response: I evaluated consoles (redwood-console/route-dashboard) and confirmed elevated token generation times across 3 of 5 serving nodes.
  - Immediate mitigation: triggered manual scale-up of dedicated burst pool (api-control -> capacity-bump endpoint). Also enabled automatic fallback policy to model variant gpt-medium-q3 in EU-region to reduce cross-region latency.
  - Outcome: traffic normalized in ~12m; error rate returned to baseline in ~14m.
  - Hypothesis: transient KV-cache thrash after a heavy sampling job from internal QA that triggered many cold-prefix streams. Logs show many 'kv_cache_miss' spikes starting 01:05 and TTL-based evictions ramping at 01:08.
  - Notes: Pagerduty incident P3001 linked.

- 03:42 UTC: Alert: elevated 429s + client-retry loops for embedding-requests endpoint (bulk embedding job from partner-corp).
  - Symptoms: steady 429 rate ~4.5% for 10 minutes, queue depth on frontend increased by ~30%. Observed many duplicate client retries (backoff not respected).
  - Mitigation: temporarily applied route-based rate limit override to reduce burst allowance for partner-corp API key; contacted partner via slack (#partner-notify) and asked to defer heavy job.
  - Outcome: 429 rate dropped to 0.4% within 9m; partner agreed to throttle and re-run during business hours. No broader customer impact.
  - Hypothesis: client-side misconfiguration + unexpected request fanout from partner testing parallelization.
  - Action item: create follow-up with partner success to implement quota-based circuit and educate on retry/backoff best practices (ticket CS-8346).

Observability notes & metrics observed:
- Console traces show KV cache miss ratio spiked to 0.78 at peak during first event (normal ~0.05).
- Serving runtime telemetry: average KV eviction rate jumped from 45 evictions/min to 610 evictions/min.
- Token generation time per step increased; kernel selection logs show switching to fallback quant paths (instrumentation note: need clearer tagging for kernel downgrade reasons).
- Sampling: our current sampling probe (1% request trace) missed the earliest spike; propose increasing sampling to 5% for 6h after an alert trigger window.

Runbook/actions taken (what worked, what didn't):
- What worked:
  - Capacity bump API reliably executed and increased headroom quickly.
  - Fallback routing to compatible model variant prevented larger SLA breaches.
  - Slack incident channel coordination concise; ops-runbook checklist useful.
- What failed / could be better:
  - Detection: p95-centric alert delayed initial detection by ~4 minutes. Need to add a short-window anomaly detector (1m rolling window) on error-rate and kv-cache-miss.
  - Runbook clarity: the 'fallback-route' playbook has ambiguous instruction about whether to also clear cache on serving nodes. I attempted a cache-clear on two nodes but was unsure if it would break ongoing sessions.
  - Partner 429 case: our rate-limit override requires manual approval in console; consider a quicker temporary throttle API for oncall use.

Follow-ups (open, owners, priority):
- SRE-FF-1: Investigate root cause of KV cache thrash; correlate QA job IDs and autoscaling events. Owner: Diego Martinez. Priority: high. Target: 2026-04-07.
- SRE-FF-2: Add short-window anomaly detector (1m) on error-rate + kv_cache_miss ratio. Owner: Jordan Kim. Priority: high. Target: 2026-04-09.
- SRE-FF-3: Runbook edits — clarify fallback routing steps and cache-clear guidance (include exact safe commands and expected side-effects). Owner: Avery Patel. Priority: medium. Target: 2026-04-08.
- CS-FF-1: Partner onboarding follow-up and quota circuity doc; coordinate with partner-success. Owner: Sasha Lopez. Priority: medium. Target: 2026-04-12.

Temporary compensating changes applied:
- Manual capacity bump applied at 01:12 (bumped 2x burst nodes). Rolled back to baseline at 02:00 after monitoring.
- Route-level throttle for partner key applied at 03:45 and removed at 04:10 after confirmation.

Runbook draft items / suggestions (notes to next shift/or infra team):
- Add a short diagnostic checklist to the 'kv-cache' runbook: how to safely check per-node evictions, safe cache-clear commands, effects on KV cold-start.
- Provide a one-click 'temporary-throttle' API for oncall (authenticated, time-limited override) to avoid manual console approval delays.
- Instrument kernel-decision traces with friendly tags (reason=kv-thrashing | reason=latency-heartbeat | reason=quant-fallback) so we can filter traces quickly.

Communication & escalation log:
- 01:20 UTC: Notified eng-monitoring channel with incident summary and initial mitigation.
- 01:25 UTC: Notified product-owner (PM) because some partner customers were in A/B tests; PM asked for a post-mortem if recurrence.
- 03:48 UTC: Slack with partner-corp engineering; agreed to defer batch and implement client-side rate-limiting.

Notes to next shift (explicit handoff):
- Monitor kv_cache_miss ratio for next 12h; if it exceeds 0.2 for >5m, escalate to Diego and consider preemptive cache-warm job.
- Jordan will start on the anomaly-detector ticket; check progress at 09:30 UTC standup.
- I will update the fallback-routing section of the runbook before EOD; if not complete, please prioritize in the morning.
- Keep an eye on any escalations tagged P3001.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why did QA job cause such synchronous cold-prefix requests? Are there new test harness changes that parallelize more than expected?
- Did autoscaler policy (scale-in delay) interact badly with cache eviction timing? Need correlation of autoscaler logs.

Attachments and references:
- Links: PagerDuty P3001, slack thread: #ops-incident-3001, trace links (console dashboard IDs included in linked_artifacts).
- Relevant runbooks: kv-cache, fallback-routing, temporary-throttle (draft).

Quick personal notes (to self):
- Reminder: capture the exact QA job id and ping the infra-qa channel. We saw a pattern of sequential prefix-pop generation at 01:04-01:09.
- Follow up with infra team on whether we can add a 'soft-warm' prefetch when new prefixes exceed threshold.

End-of-shift status: system baseline restored; incident P3001 is resolved (monitoring only). Partner 429 case resolved with partner agreement. Several follow-ups created with owners and reasonable SLAs. Handoff complete.

Signed,
Avery P.
